odhad-nemovitosti-pro-dedicke-rizeni.title: I need a property valuation for inheritance proceedings. What should I do?
odhad-nemovitosti-pro-dedicke-rizeni.seoTitle: Property valuation for inheritance in the Czech Republic | Ing. Aleš Vachuška
odhad-nemovitosti-pro-dedicke-rizeni.description: How to arrange a property valuation for a Czech notary handling an inheritance, how the valuation works and which documents are needed.
odhad-nemovitosti-pro-dedicke-rizeni.cardDescription: What to prepare and how the valuation works.
odhad-nemovitosti-pro-dedicke-rizeni.intro: If an estate includes property in the Czech Republic (a house, holiday home, apartment or land), the notary will require evidence of its market value. A written property valuation is generally used for this purpose.

blocks.text: What is needed for the valuation?
To begin with, the property needs to be identified:

items: **House or apartment:** address, or the ownership sheet number (LV) and cadastral area.
**Land:** ownership sheet number (LV) and the relevant cadastral area.
**Other properties:** agricultural buildings, workshops and other structures can be identified by their parcel number and cadastral area.

**Several properties:** for example, a house together with agricultural or forest land. In this case, the ownership sheet numbers (LV) and the relevant cadastral areas are the most useful starting point.

blocks.text: Any further information and documents needed will be clarified as necessary.
For Czech inheritance proceedings, the property is valued as at the date of death.
How do I prepare the valuation?
I use actual sale prices of comparable properties, rather than relying only on asking prices in property listings.

A valuation for inheritance proceedings has a shorter structure than a full valuation report. **The value calculation itself usually remains the same.** I mainly reduce the length of the document, rather than changing the valuation approach.
The fee depends on the scope of the valuation and the documents available. We always agree the specific fee before work begins.
Complete the contact form below and I will get back to you, or call me.

kolik-stoji-odhad-pro-dedicke-rizeni.title: How much does a property valuation for inheritance proceedings cost?
kolik-stoji-odhad-pro-dedicke-rizeni.seoTitle: Inheritance property valuation fees in the Czech Republic | Ing. Aleš Vachuška
kolik-stoji-odhad-pro-dedicke-rizeni.description: What determines the fee for a property valuation for a Czech inheritance case, and how the price is agreed before work begins.
kolik-stoji-odhad-pro-dedicke-rizeni.cardDescription: What affects the scope of work and the valuation fee.
kolik-stoji-odhad-pro-dedicke-rizeni.intro: The valuation fee is agreed individually according to the type of property and the scope of the work. Valuing a standard apartment involves different work from valuing a house with several plots or a group of agricultural properties.

blocks.text: How is the valuation fee determined?

To quote a fee, I first need to know what the property is, where it is located and the valuation date (the date of death). For several properties, it is best to provide the ownership sheet numbers (LV) and the relevant cadastral areas.
Based on this information, I assess the scope of work and quote a specific fee, which we **always agree before work begins**.
What does the valuation contain?

A valuation for Czech inheritance proceedings has a shorter structure than a full valuation report. The value calculation itself usually remains the same and is based on actual sales of comparable properties.

odhad-pro-dedictvi-bez-prohlidky.title: Can a property be valued for inheritance without an on-site inspection?
odhad-pro-dedictvi-bez-prohlidky.seoTitle: Inheritance valuation without an inspection in the Czech Republic
odhad-pro-dedictvi-bez-prohlidky.description: When photographs and documents allow a Czech inheritance valuation without an inspection, and when a more detailed assessment is appropriate.
odhad-pro-dedictvi-bez-prohlidky.cardDescription: When available documents can be sufficient for a valuation.
odhad-pro-dedictvi-bez-prohlidky.intro: Yes, in many cases a valuation for Czech inheritance proceedings can be prepared without an on-site inspection. This mainly depends on the property and the documents available.

blocks.text: Which documents are needed?
**Houses, apartments, holiday homes and other buildings**

The condition of these properties has a significant effect on their value. I therefore send clients a short questionnaire and ask for selected photographs. In many cases, this information allows me to prepare a valuation without an on-site inspection.
**Land**

For land, I can generally use Czech cadastral records, the municipality’s land-use planning documents and the public Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS). Further information may be needed depending on the type of land.
When is an on-site inspection needed?
Mainly when the available documents do not allow a sufficient assessment of the condition, extent of the buildings or their actual use.
If the information is insufficient, we agree on additional documents or an on-site inspection.
When should you choose a more detailed valuation?

If you only need a valuation for inheritance proceedings, I aim to keep the process as straightforward as possible. The report is shorter and avoids unnecessarily lengthy descriptions. **The value calculation and comparison with actual sales are still retained.**

However, if you already know that you will later sell the property, buy out other co-owners, divide assets or use the valuation for another property decision, I recommend considering a full, more detailed valuation with an on-site inspection.
This allows a closer assessment of the actual condition, fittings and any defects. The resulting report can then be used both for inheritance proceedings and as a basis for subsequent decisions.
It is therefore best to agree the scope of the valuation in advance according to its intended purpose.

podklady-pro-odhad-nemovitosti-dedictvi.title: Which documents do I need for an inheritance property valuation?
podklady-pro-odhad-nemovitosti-dedictvi.seoTitle: Documents for a Czech inheritance property valuation
podklady-pro-odhad-nemovitosti-dedictvi.description: The property details, ownership sheets, cadastral areas, photographs and date of death needed for a valuation for a Czech notary.
podklady-pro-odhad-nemovitosti-dedictvi.cardDescription: The details and documents needed for the valuation.
podklady-pro-odhad-nemovitosti-dedictvi.intro: Basic property details are enough for the initial discussion. We can clarify any further documents needed afterwards.

blocks.text: What is needed?

items: **House or apartment:** address, or the ownership sheet number (LV) and cadastral area.
**Land:** ownership sheet number (LV) and the relevant cadastral area.
**Other buildings:** parcel number and cadastral area.
**Several properties:** the ownership sheet numbers (LV) and their cadastral areas.

blocks.text: For houses, apartments and other buildings, I send a short questionnaire about their condition and ask for selected photographs.
I can look up further details where possible, or we can fill in the missing information together.

odhad-nebo-znalecky-posudek-dedictvi.title: Is a formal expert report necessary for inheritance proceedings?
odhad-nebo-znalecky-posudek-dedictvi.seoTitle: Valuation or formal expert report for a Czech inheritance case?
odhad-nebo-znalecky-posudek-dedictvi.description: The difference between a property valuer’s written valuation and a formal expert report for inheritance proceedings in the Czech Republic.
odhad-nebo-znalecky-posudek-dedictvi.cardDescription: The difference between a valuation and a formal expert report.
odhad-nebo-znalecky-posudek-dedictvi.intro: **An ordinary Czech inheritance case does not usually require a formal expert report.** A written valuation by a property valuer may be sufficient evidence of market value.

blocks.text: What is the difference?
A formal expert report is prepared by a legally authorised expert under the Czech rules governing expert work. It may be required, for example, in more complex or disputed cases.
A written valuation by a property valuer is a professional assessment that may serve as a basis for determining market value in inheritance proceedings.
How do I prepare the valuation?
I use actual sales of comparable properties and account for the differences that affect their value.
A valuation for inheritance proceedings has a shorter structure than a full valuation report, but **the value calculation itself usually remains the same**.
The result is therefore not just an indicative figure, but a written valuation with a documented calculation and an explanation of the assessed value.

odhad-pozemku-pro-dedicke-rizeni.title: Land valuation for inheritance proceedings
odhad-pozemku-pro-dedicke-rizeni.seoTitle: Land valuation for inheritance in the Czech Republic | Ing. Aleš Vachuška
odhad-pozemku-pro-dedicke-rizeni.description: Valuations of farmland, meadows, gardens, building plots, forest land and co-ownership shares for Czech inheritance proceedings.
odhad-pozemku-pro-dedicke-rizeni.cardDescription: Valuing farmland, gardens, building plots and ownership shares.
odhad-pozemku-pro-dedicke-rizeni.intro: An estate may also include land, such as arable land, meadows, gardens, building plots or forest land. There may be many parcels, or only co-ownership shares.

blocks.text: How is land valued?
I use actual sales of comparable land, taking particular account of location, area, access and possible uses.
The land-use plan is also important. A parcel recorded as arable land in the Czech cadastre may, for example, be designated for future development, which significantly affects its value.
What if there are several plots?
One valuation can cover a larger group of plots recorded on several ownership sheets, including co-ownership shares.
To begin with, I need the **ownership sheet numbers (LV) and the relevant cadastral areas**. I can use these details to find the individual parcels and their basic information.
For Czech inheritance proceedings, the land is valued as at the date of death.

cena-nemovitosti-ke-dni-umrti.title: How is a property’s value at the date of death determined?
cena-nemovitosti-ke-dni-umrti.seoTitle: Property value at the date of death for a Czech inheritance case
cena-nemovitosti-ke-dni-umrti.description: How a Czech inheritance valuation reflects comparable sales, property characteristics and price changes when valuing at the date of death.
cena-nemovitosti-ke-dni-umrti.cardDescription: Why the valuation relates to a specific date.
cena-nemovitosti-ke-dni-umrti.intro: In Czech inheritance proceedings, property is valued as at the date of death. This is the relevant date for determining market value, regardless of when the valuation is actually prepared.

blocks.text: How does the valuation work?
To determine market value, I use actual sales of comparable properties. I account for their location, size, condition and other characteristics that affect the resulting value.
If the valuation is prepared a considerable time after the death, I also account for property price changes over the relevant period.
What do I need for the valuation?
To begin with, I need the basic property identification details and the date of death.
For houses, apartments and other buildings, I may ask for information about their condition and selected photographs. We clarify any further details according to the particular property.

odhad-nemovitosti-pri-rozvodu.title: Property valuation for divorce and division of marital property
odhad-nemovitosti-pri-rozvodu.seoTitle: Property valuation for divorce in the Czech Republic
odhad-nemovitosti-pri-rozvodu.description: A written valuation of Czech property as a basis for dividing marital assets, buying out a spouse or negotiating a settlement.
odhad-nemovitosti-pri-rozvodu.cardDescription: A valuation as a basis for a property settlement.
odhad-nemovitosti-pri-rozvodu.intro:
If Czech marital community property (SJ, previously recorded in the cadastre as SJM) includes a house, apartment, land or other property, its value needs to be established when the spouses divorce.

A written valuation can provide a basis for an agreement on dividing assets, buying out one spouse or further negotiations on a property settlement.

blocks.text: How do I determine the property’s value?
I mainly use actual sales of comparable properties, rather than relying only on asking prices in property listings.
For houses and apartments, I assess location, size, layout, condition and any renovations in particular.
For land, the main factors are location, area, access and possible uses under the land-use plan.
The result is a written valuation with a calculation and an explanation of the assessed value.
How can a valuation help with a property settlement?
For example, if one spouse keeps the house and the other is to receive financial compensation, it is important to know the property value on which their agreement is based.
A valuation can also cover several properties at once, such as a house, a holiday property and separate plots of land.
The valuation does not determine how assets should be divided under the law. It provides a professionally supported value for further negotiations and a possible agreement.
What do I need to prepare a valuation?
To begin with, the properties need to be identified:

items: **House or apartment:** address, or the ownership sheet number (LV) and cadastral area.
**Land:** ownership sheet number (LV) and the relevant cadastral area.
**Several properties:** the ownership sheet numbers (LV) and their cadastral areas.

blocks.text: It is also important to clarify whether the valuation is needed for an agreement, financial compensation or ongoing Czech court proceedings. We use its purpose to agree the appropriate scope and valuation date.
For houses, apartments and other buildings, I recommend an on-site inspection to assess their actual condition more closely.
We always agree the specific valuation fee before work begins.

vyplaceni-spoluvlastnickeho-podilu.title: Buying out a co-ownership share in a property
vyplaceni-spoluvlastnickeho-podilu.seoTitle: Property valuation for buying out a co-owner in the Czech Republic
vyplaceni-spoluvlastnickeho-podilu.description: How to value Czech property for a co-owner buyout, and how this differs from valuing a share for a separate sale.
vyplaceni-spoluvlastnickeho-podilu.cardDescription: How to value a property and establish the value of a share.
vyplaceni-spoluvlastnickeho-podilu.intro:
If a property has several owners and one wishes to buy out the others, it is important to establish its value first.

Typically, this concerns a house, apartment, holiday property or land co-owned by siblings or other relatives.

blocks.text: How is the buyout amount determined?
A settlement between co-owners usually starts from the value of the whole property and the size of each co-ownership share.
For example, if a house is worth CZK 4,000,000 and two siblings each own one half, the value corresponding to each share is CZK 2,000,000.

A different situation arises when a co-ownership share is sold separately to a third party. Its market value may be lower than the corresponding proportion of the whole property’s value, because the buyer does not acquire exclusive ownership of the property.
It is therefore important to clarify the purpose of the valuation in advance.
How do I value the property?
I determine the value using actual sales of comparable properties.
For houses, apartments and holiday properties, I assess location, size, condition and other characteristics affecting the price.
For land, I mainly account for location, area, access and possible uses.
The result is a written valuation with a calculation and an explanation of the assessed value.
What do I need to prepare a valuation?
To begin with, the property needs to be identified:

items: **House or apartment:** address, or the ownership sheet number (LV) and cadastral area.
**Land:** ownership sheet number (LV) and the relevant cadastral area.
**Several properties:** the ownership sheet numbers (LV) and their cadastral areas.

blocks.text: It is also useful to state whether the valuation concerns a buyout between co-owners or a share intended for a separate sale.
We always agree the scope and fee before work begins.

rozdeleni-nemovitosti-mezi-spoluvlastnik.title: Dividing properties between co-owners
rozdeleni-nemovitosti-mezi-spoluvlastnik.seoTitle: Valuing Czech properties for division between co-owners
rozdeleni-nemovitosti-mezi-spoluvlastnik.description: A written valuation of several Czech properties provides a basis for their division and any financial adjustment between co-owners.
rozdeleni-nemovitosti-mezi-spoluvlastnik.cardDescription: Valuing several properties as a basis for an agreement.
rozdeleni-nemovitosti-mezi-spoluvlastnik.intro:
A settlement of jointly owned assets often involves several properties at once, such as a house, apartment, holiday property or several plots of land.

A written valuation establishes the value of each property and provides a basis for dividing them between the co-owners.

blocks.text: How can a valuation help?
I value each property separately according to its characteristics and actual sales of comparable properties.
The result is a breakdown of the individual property values and their combined value.

The valuation can be used, for example, for an agreement in which one co-owner takes the house and another takes land or a different property. If the values of the transferred assets differ, the agreement may also include financial compensation.
What do I need for the valuation?
To begin with, property addresses or **ownership sheet numbers (LV) and the relevant cadastral areas** are sufficient.
We then clarify which properties should be valued and whether the valuation is for an agreement between the co-owners or another purpose.

za-kolik-prodat-nemovitost.title: What price should I sell my property for?
za-kolik-prodat-nemovitost.seoTitle: Setting a selling price for property in the Czech Republic
za-kolik-prodat-nemovitost.description: Why asking prices alone are not enough when setting a selling price for a Czech house, apartment or plot of land.
za-kolik-prodat-nemovitost.cardDescription: Why property listings alone are not enough to set a price.
za-kolik-prodat-nemovitost.intro: If you plan to sell a house, apartment or plot of land, one of the first questions is what asking price to set.

blocks.text: How can you establish the property’s actual value?
Prices are often based on similar properties advertised on property portals. However, those listings mainly show the sellers’ asking prices, rather than the amounts the properties actually sold for.
I therefore base the valuation on actual sales of comparable properties.
For houses and apartments, I mainly consider location, size, condition and fittings. For land, the main factors are location, area, access and possible uses.
What can the valuation be used for?
The result is a written valuation with a calculation and an explanation of the assessed value.
The valuation can provide a basis for setting the asking price and help avoid advertising the property at an unreasonably high or unnecessarily low price.
The final sale price may differ depending on current demand, the method of sale and negotiations with prospective buyers.

odhad-ceny-nemovitosti-pred-koupi.title: Buying a property? How can you tell if the price is too high?
odhad-ceny-nemovitosti-pred-koupi.seoTitle: Property valuation before buying in the Czech Republic
odhad-ceny-nemovitosti-pred-koupi.description: Compare the asking price of a Czech house, apartment or plot with a valuation based on actual sales of comparable properties.
odhad-ceny-nemovitosti-pred-koupi.cardDescription: Comparing the asking price with actual property sales.
odhad-ceny-nemovitosti-pred-koupi.intro: When buying a house, apartment or plot of land, it may be difficult to judge whether the asking price reflects its actual value.

blocks.text: How can you assess whether the price is reasonable?
Property listings can provide an initial guide. However, the difference between asking prices and actual sale prices can reach 10%, and in some cases 20% or more.
I therefore mainly use actual sales of comparable properties. These provide a more reliable basis for determining value than asking prices alone.
For houses and apartments, I mainly account for location, size, layout, condition and fittings. For land, I consider location, area, access and possible uses.
What can the valuation be used for?
The result is a written valuation that allows you to compare the asking purchase price with a professionally assessed property value.
If these amounts differ significantly, the valuation can also support price negotiations with the seller.

jak-zjistit-hodnotu-nemovitosti.title: How can you find out the current value of your property?
jak-zjistit-hodnotu-nemovitosti.seoTitle: Current property value in the Czech Republic: an individual valuation
jak-zjistit-hodnotu-nemovitosti.description: How an individual valuation of Czech property differs from an online calculator, and when a written valuation can be useful.
jak-zjistit-hodnotu-nemovitosti.cardDescription: When knowing the value of your own property is useful.
jak-zjistit-hodnotu-nemovitosti.intro: You do not have to be selling a property to need to know its value. A valuation may be useful, for example, when distributing assets among your children or other relatives during your lifetime, making family agreements, considering investments or simply keeping track of your assets.

blocks.text: Online calculator or individual valuation?

Online calculators generally use limited property information. They usually account for location, area, type and a few other basic details. However, they may not adequately assess the actual condition, renovations, fittings or other specific characteristics.
The result is therefore often a fairly broad price range that gives only an approximate indication of value.
Some online calculators are also mainly intended to provide a quick preliminary estimate, followed by an offer to arrange a sale.
How is an individual valuation different?
I base the valuation on actual sales of comparable properties, rather than relying only on asking prices in property listings.

For houses, apartments and holiday homes, an on-site inspection allows a closer assessment of actual condition, quality of construction, fittings and any renovations. This helps evaluate differences between the property being valued and comparable sales more precisely.
For land, I mainly account for location, area, access and possible uses under the land-use planning documents.
The result is a **written valuation with a specific assessed value, a clear calculation and an explanation**, rather than just an automatically generated price range.
